tagline: Runtime firewall for AI agents — blocks prompt injection before your agent reads it
description_md:
# AEGIS — runtime firewall for AI agents

AEGIS inspects untrusted content reaching your agent — inbox messages, tool results, web fetches, MCP responses, skill files, memory notes — and blocks **prompt injection, jailbreaks, and impersonation** before the agent ever sees it. Genuine status messages pass straight through.

## How it works

Two layers. **L1** is Aho-Corasick pattern matching in pure Rust — microseconds, ~120 known attack families with homoglyph and leetspeak normalization and a sliding-window scan. **L2** is an optional local Qwen3-1.7B judge via llama.cpp — fully offline, no network. On a held-out labeled set: **90% recall, 95% precision, 92% F1**. An 880 KB binary with an HMAC-chained audit log at `~/.aegis/audit.jsonl`.

## Using it

- `aegis.scan <path>` — one-shot scan of a file or directory.
- `aegis.exec {"args":["scan-cmd"],"stdin":...}` — the PreToolUse blocking gate (exit 0 allow / 2 block).
- `aegis.exec {"args":["scan-result"],"stdin":...}` — the PostToolUse non-blocking check (warns).
- `aegis.status` / `aegis.targets` / `aegis.config` — audit log, protected surfaces, and configuration.

The L2 judge model (~1.8 GB) is optional — L1 patterns work without it.

methods.name: aegis.scan
methods.summary: One-shot scan of one or more files or directories for prompt injection, jailbreaks, homoglyph/leetspeak obfuscation, and impersonation. Returns the verdict per path. This is `aegis scan <path>...`.

methods.name: aegis.status
methods.summary: Tail the HMAC-chained audit log of recent verdicts. This is `aegis status`.

methods.name: aegis.targets
methods.summary: List the agent surfaces AEGIS is protecting (inbox, tool results, skill files, memory, ...). This is `aegis targets`.

methods.name: aegis.config
methods.summary: Show the effective AEGIS configuration (rules, thresholds, watch targets). This is `aegis config`.

methods.name: aegis.version
methods.summary: Print the AEGIS version. This is `aegis version`.

methods.name: aegis.exec
methods.summary: Run any AEGIS subcommand with a verbatim argv — the full surface beyond the curated methods. Payload is {"args":[<subcommand>, ...]} with optional {"stdin":"..."}. This is how you use the blocking gates: the PreToolUse gate {"args":["scan-cmd"],"stdin":"{\"tool_input\":{\"command\":\"...\"}}"} exits 0 (allow) or 2 (block); the PostToolUse gate {"args":["scan-result"],"stdin":"{...}"} warns without blocking. Also reaches init/daemon/install-models/install-hooks.

methods.name: aegis.help
methods.summary: Print the AEGIS usage and subcommand list. This is `aegis --help`.

methods.name: aegis.help
methods.summary: Discovery: every method with params, kind, and latency class.

gotchas: Fully offline: L1 Aho-Corasick patterns need no network; the L2 judge model (~1.8 GB) is optional.
aegis.scan takes a filesystem path, not raw text — write the content to a file first, then scan it.
scan-cmd (via aegis.exec) is the blocking gate: exit 0 = allow, 2 = block; scan-result warns without blocking.
Verdicts append to an HMAC-chained audit log at ~/.aegis/audit.jsonl — read it with aegis.status.
